subject: Climate & Environment
title: Floods and Droughts from Clearing
description: Learn Floods and Droughts from Clearing in one minute.

hook.text: Forests act like giant sponges — absorbing rain and releasing it slowly into rivers.

buildup.text: Tree roots create channels in the soil that help water seep underground gradually.

discovery.text: Without forests, rain runs off bare ground instantly, swelling rivers into flash floods.

twist.text: The same cleared land that floods in the wet season bakes dry in summer — no stored water left.

climax.text: Deforested watersheds swing between floods and droughts. The buffer zone is gone.

punchline.text: Forests are flood insurance that grows on trees.

quiz.question: How do forests prevent flooding?
options: They absorb rain and release it slowly

details.summary: Deforestation amplifies both floods and droughts by removing the natural water regulation that forests provide. Without tree cover, rain runs off rapidly causing flash floods, while groundwater recharge and dry-season stream flow decline, worsening drought.
details.whyItMatters: Billions of people depend on forested watersheds for water supply. Deforestation converts steady water flows into destructive boom-and-bust cycles.
takeaways: Deforested watersheds experience more intense peak flooding
Groundwater recharge drops when forests are cleared, reducing dry-season flow
Sedimentation from eroded soil fills reservoirs and clogs rivers

faq.question: How does deforestation increase flood risk?
faq.answer: Forest canopy intercepts rain, root systems hold soil, and organic soils absorb water. Removing these buffers means rain hits bare ground, creating rapid surface runoff that overwhelms rivers and causes flash floods downstream.

faq.question: Can reforestation restore hydrological function?
faq.answer: Yes, but it takes decades for soil structure, root depth, and organic matter to rebuild. Fast-growing monoculture plantations may not provide the same water regulation as diverse native forests due to shallower roots and different transpiration patterns.
